task: Get a reminder to call the camp director about Rafi's waitlist, and see whether the app can help you follow up with the camp.
transcript: Opened the app: a Home screen asking 'What can I help with?' with example prompts and a note that nothing is sent without my OK.
Typed 'Remind me to call the camp director about Rafi's waitlist' and pressed enter; it showed 'Getting started' then 'Sending'.

Waited 30 seconds: it set a reminder for Mon Nov 16 at 10am to call Marcy Feld, the Camp Kaylie director, showed her number (845) 555-0142, and summarized that Rafi was #4 on the Session 2 waitlist as of Oct 20 and that my Nov 1 email got no reply. It offered to change the day or time.
Typed 'can you help me follow up with the camp? maybe write her an email' and pressed enter; it showed 'Working on it'.

Waited about 90 seconds in total: a 'Draft email, not sent' appeared, addressed to marcy@campkaylie.test, subject 'Re: Rafi Levin - Session 2 waitlist', with a friendly follow-up asking about Rafi's Session 2 spot, other sessions, and offering a phone call, plus 'Open in Mail' and 'Copy' buttons.
Tapped 'Open in Mail', which hands the draft to my own mail app; the screen stayed on the draft.
stumbles: The draft took about a minute and a half with only 'Working on it' and dots, slower than ChatGPT.
It picked Monday at 10am for the reminder without asking; fine for me, but it was a choice made for me (it did offer to change it).
After tapping 'Open in Mail' the app screen looked the same, so on a phone I would rely on the mail app popping up to know it worked.
verdict: This felt like ChatGPT that actually knows my email: one sentence got a reminder with the director's name, number and where the waitlist stands, and one more got a ready follow-up email. It never sent anything on its own and the only drag was waiting about a minute and a half for the draft.
